reasons: Rule scope is satisfied: Section 7.2 binds Customer (must disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider), which is a right-of-first-refusal restraint on Customer's freedom to source from other suppliers — squarely the restrictive-covenant harm the rule targets, and not exclusivity granted in Customer's favour.

Deviation status is correct and well-supported: the clause has no product/category limit, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit, so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions; it also conflicts with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no exclusivity or MFC commitment.

Redline is directionally correct and minimal: deleting only p0026 removes the entire offending obligation without touching unrelated terms, and no residual sole-supplier/requirements language remains (consistent with the deterministic checks).

Comment complies with tone and content requirements — concise, first person plural, [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the Section 12.3 conflict, and offers the category-limited/12-month/performance-exit fallback without lecturing.
Correctly scopes out the Section 2.1 take-or-pay minimum as a separate volume-commitment issue rather than over-editing under this rule.
